metadata.note: The Boston, Hoosac Tunnel and Western Railway (New York 1877, Vermont 1878, consolidated 1880): Gen. William L. Burt's line from the Massachusetts-Vermont state line west of Williamstown, at the end of the Commonwealth's Troy & Greenfield, through Pownal VT, Hoosick Falls and Johnsonville to Mechanicville (opened 22 Dec 1879), extended to the West Shore at Rotterdam Junction (1884), with the leased Saratoga Springs branch (1882). Fitchburg control 1887 (merger 1 Oct 1892), Boston and Maine lease 1900. Drawn as one feature per drawable span x operator (CLAUDE.md Rule 4 splits share geometry): BHT&W 1879-1887, Fitchburg 1887-1900, Boston and Maine 1900-. The main line is cut at Johnsonville because the evidence differs on the two sides: east of it the BHT&W track carried the B&M's Boston - Troy trains to Jan 1958; west of it the last confirmed passenger year is 1906. Built from research/branches/boston_hoosac_tunnel_and_western_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-16).
metadata.colour_note: Boston and Maine Railroad colour pulled programmatically from the existing 'Boston and Maine Railroad' features in data/ (#1D3557). 'Fitchburg Railroad' and 'Boston, Hoosac Tunnel and Western Railway' had no features in data/; their new colours (#7A3B69, #8E2C48) were checked programmatically to be unused by any other company. Later Fitchburg-era features elsewhere (Troy & Boston 1887-1900, Cheshire 1890-1900, the Fitchburg main) should reuse #7A3B69.
omitted: Report block [8], Saratoga Lake Railway (own operation, Saratoga Springs - Saratoga Lake, 1881-1882): HELD under Rule 5. The report could not confirm its motive power -- it was a 'rapid transit road' (New-York Tribune 10 Jul 1881) and steam is likely but not established (report UNRESOLVED 5). Not drawn until steam (or other mechanical traction) is sourced.

Report block [12], Schuylerville Branch (Schuyler Junction - Schuylerville, 7.9 mi): drawable NONE -- no confirmed passenger year (Fowler's 1882 Appleton's Guide station names are the best lead, report UNRESOLVED 4).

Report block [13], Troy & Greenfield North Adams - State Line: not a BHT&W block (BHT&W trains used it by agreement); belongs to a Troy & Greenfield / Fitchburg file. Nothing here draws east of the MA/VT state line.
Saratoga & Schuylerville Railroad (1946-1956/57): freight-only short line successor on the Saratoga branch (Rule 1).
Johnsonville - Rotterdam Junction after 1906 and the Saratoga branch after 1901: not drawn -- no passenger evidence found either way; the drawn ends are [OPEN].
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1: every feature ends at its last confirmed passenger year or operator change; the post-1906 B&M freight main west of Johnsonville, post-1958 freight east of it and the freight-only Saratoga & Schuylerville are mentioned in notes only.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Built to Rule 5: the Saratoga Lake Railway (1881-82), whose motive power is unconfirmed, is held back (see omitted). Nothing else in the file was animal-powered.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] END: Boston and Maine Johnsonville - Mechanicville - Rotterdam Junction (bm-johnsonville-rotterdam-junction) drawn to 1906, the last confirmed year (Wabash tourist cars via Rotterdam Junction). No source dates the end of through cars or of any local train at Schaghticoke, Reynolds, Mechanicville, Ushers, Elnora or Scotia. Official Guides c.1910-1930, Chronicling America 1907-1940, BMRRHS discontinuance files are the next sources.
[OPEN][ANCHOR]: Boston and Maine Saratoga Springs Branch (bm-saratoga-springs-branch) drawn 1901 only, and that anchor rests on a presumed routing of a Worcester - Saratoga excursion.
[ANCHOR]: Fitchburg Saratoga Springs Branch (fitchburg-saratoga-springs-branch) drawn 1894 only; regular Fitchburg trains 1887-1900 likely but no timetable seen.

[OPEN] START: BHT&W Mechanicville - Rotterdam Junction drawn from 1885 (first confirmed passenger cars), not the 1884 opening; 1884 (Wikipedia, American-Rails) vs 1879 (JBVB, Wikipedia Freight Subdivision) opening conflict unresolved.

Which of the two parallel alignments between the state line and Johnsonville is the BHT&W-built one is inferred, not proven (report UNRESOLVED 2): the existing Troy & Boston layer draws the abandoned grade, so this layer draws the surviving main track. When each stretch of the other alignment lost its trains is not established.
1879 mileage conflict: 46 miles opened (SWR79) vs 38 (Wikipedia); Fowler's mileposts support ~38-40.
Month of the 1887 Fitchburg takeover of the BHT&W not established ('shortly after' 3 May 1887).
Whether BHT&W passenger trains ran through over the D&H to Schenectady 1879-1884, and whether BHT&W crews worked east of North Adams.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

PARALLEL-LINE CHECK (report UNRESOLVED 2): the existing Troy & Boston feature troy-boston-hoosick-valley draws the abandoned T&B grade ('Troy & Boston RR' / 'old B&M alignment') west of the NY/VT line; this trace stays on the other, surviving alignment. segments.note: Report block [1]. Gen. William L. Burt's new line from the Massachusetts-Vermont state line west of Williamstown (end of the state-owned Troy & Greenfield) through Pownal and North Pownal VT, Petersburgh Junction, Hoosick, Hoosick Falls, Hoosick Junction, Eagle Bridge and Buskirk to Johnsonville NY, built in the teeth of 30-40 lawsuits from the parallel Troy & Boston. Formally opened Monday 22 Dec 1879 with excursion trains from Troy and from Boston; the company then owned 7 engines and 10 first-class passenger cars (Springfield Weekly Republican 26 Dec 1879, primary). A BHT&W train was derailed at Hoosick Falls in July 1881 (New-York Tribune 27 Jul 1881, train type not stated); in Oct 1884 a BHT&W '8.30 express train west' is reported and the Fitchburg and BHT&W jointly petitioned for an added Sunday passenger train (Springfield Weekly Republican 10 Oct 1884). Through traffic was handed to the Fitchburg at North Adams; BHT&W trains reached North Adams over the Troy & Greenfield, which is not drawn here. Ends 1887 with Fitchburg control (the Fitchburg bought the Troy & Boston 3 May 1887 and 'shortly afterward' took control of the BHT&W; month not established) -- an operator change, not a service end. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no public timetable was read for frequency).
sources: Segment-level: opening 22 Dec 1879 from SWR79 (primary) and Wikipedia; 1881 and 1884 trains from NYT81c and SWR84 (primary); 1887 operator change from Wikipedia. Compiled in research/branches/boston_hoosac_tunnel_and_western_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-16)

segments.note: Report block [2]. The BHT&W-built track under the Fitchburg Railroad, which took control in 1887 (BHT&W formally merged into it 1 Oct 1892 -- not a second split, the Fitchburg already ran the trains). From 1887 the BHT&W and Troy & Boston lines between Williamstown and Johnsonville 'were operated as a single line' (Wikipedia), i.e. as a directional double track, so this track carried passenger trains in at least one direction; the New-York Tribune of 25 Dec 1887 gives the Fitchburg double track Boston - Johnsonville. Direct passenger evidence: a Fitchburg Sunday special of 5 Aug 1894 left Pownal and stopped 'at all stations between Reynolds and North Adams' (Bennington Semi-Weekly Banner 3 Aug 1894); Boston - Chicago sleeping cars 'via Hoosac Tunnel, West Shore, Grand Trunk' in 1893 (Olneyville Times 4 Aug 1893). Both ends are operator changes (1887 Fitchburg control; 1900 Boston and Maine lease). WHICH of the two parallel alignments carried which direction, and when, is not established (report UNRESOLVED 2). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no public timetable was read for frequency).

segments.note: Report block [3]. The BHT&W-built track under the Boston and Maine, which leased the Fitchburg in 1900. It carried the B&M's Boston - Troy service (Williamstown - Pownal - Petersburgh Jn - Hoosick Jn - Johnsonville, then the old Troy & Boston to Troy), from 15 May 1926 the Minute Man; the Feb 1952 Official Guide's through-car list still shows Minute Man coaches Boston - Troy. The Minute Man last ran 18 Jan 1958 (JBVB, 'Passenger service ended 18-Jan-1958'; American-Rails gives the Troy - Williamstown cut as 19 Jan 1958), and all of this feature lies west of Williamstown, which itself kept trains to 30 Dec 1958. JBVB describes 'separated mains between State Line Tower and Johnsonville' in the steam era, so both alignments carried passenger trains well into the B&M years; when they were reduced to one is not established. Freight continued after 1958 (today's Pan Am Southern / Berkshire & Eastern main) -- context only, not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no public timetable was read for frequency).

segments.note: Report block [4]. The original western end of the 1879 line, Johnsonville - (West) Valley Falls - Schaghticoke - Reynolds - Mechanicville, connecting with the D&H (Rensselaer & Saratoga) at Mechanicville; 12.9 mi by Fowler's B&M mileposts. Opened 22 Dec 1879 -- the opening train ran from Mechanicville, where 'a number of North Adams people met the party' (Springfield Weekly Republican 26 Dec 1879). From July 1882 the route of the Boston - Saratoga trains (New-York Tribune 4 Jul 1882) and from 1885 of the West Shore through cars (Indianapolis Journal 2 Apr 1885), both of which had to use it; Valley Falls carries Fowler's 'q' (listed in the 1884 Official Guide). Whether BHT&W passenger trains ran on over the D&H to Schenectady in 1881-84 was not established. Ends 1887 with Fitchburg control (operator change). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no public timetable was read for frequency).

segments.note: Report block [5]. The Rotterdam extension, Mechanicville - Ushers - Elnora - Scotia - Rotterdam Junction (West Shore connection), 23 mi (Wikipedia; Fowler 22.4 mi). The line opened 'in early 1884' (Wikipedia, American-Rails; JBVB and the Freight Subdivision article print 1879, which conflicts with Wikipedia, American-Rails and SWR79). The START YEAR 1885 IS THE FIRST CONFIRMED PASSENGER YEAR, NOT THE OPENING: in April 1885 Pullman buffet parlor and sleeping cars ran through 'over the West Shore Hoosac Tunnel route' to Eagle Bridge, Hoosick Junction, North Adams ... Boston (Indianapolis Journal 2 Apr 1885), which can only mean via Rotterdam Junction and this line. Passenger trains in 1884 are unproven; do not move the start earlier without a source. Ends 1887 with Fitchburg control (operator change). Headway is an ESTIMATE for a through-car route; no timetable was read.

segments.note: Report block [7]. Johnsonville - Mechanicville - Rotterdam Junction under the Boston and Maine from the 1900 Fitchburg lease. END IS [OPEN]: passenger service is confirmed to 1906 by Wabash advertisements for Boston - Chicago tourist cars on the 'Continental Limited', Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, 'which New York passengers can take at Rotterdam Junction' (Among the Clouds, summer 1905 and 26 Jul 1906); those cars had to traverse this whole feature. 1906 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end -- no source dates when the through cars or any local train stopped. Do not extend without evidence, and in particular do not extend it to 1958 on the strength of the Troy route's end, which concerns a different line. A B&M Worcester - Saratoga excursion of 17 Aug 1901 (Worcester Spy 14 Aug 1901) is a further anchor for Johnsonville - Mechanicville if it used the B&M's own Saratoga branch. Later B&M employee timetables and 1960s 'Fitchburg to Rotterdam Junction' listings are freight-era and not passenger evidence; the line was the B&M's freight main to the West Shore/NYC and D&H (context only). headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the three-days-a-week tourist cars; no public timetable was read.

segments.note: Report block [9]. Mechanicville (East Saratoga Junction) - Stillwater - Wayville (Ketchum's Corners) - Cedar Bluffs - Saratoga Lake - Schuyler Junction - Eureka Springs - Saratoga Springs, 18.7 mi (Fowler). Leased by the BHT&W in July 1882 (the Saratoga Lake Railway and the Hoosac Tunnel & Saratoga; consolidated 1886 as the Troy, Saratoga & Northern -- a lessor change only, the BHT&W still ran the trains, so not split). Opened 1882: 'Saratoga and Boston special trains over the new Saratoga Springs branch of the Boston, Hoosac Tunnel and Western Railway, commence their regular trips on Wednesday' (New-York Tribune 4 Jul 1882, i.e. Wed 5 Jul 1882). A BHT&W train was stalled by snow 'between here [Saratoga] and Stillwater' in Feb 1884 (New-York Tribune 1 Mar 1884, train type not stated), and Ketchum's Corners carries Fowler's 'q' (listed in the 1884 Official Guide). Ends 1887 with Fitchburg control (operator change). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no public timetable was read for frequency).

segments.note: Report block [10]. [ANCHOR] -- a single proven year. Fitchburg Sunday special of 5 Aug 1894: Pownal 7.50 a.m., Saratoga Lake 9.50, Saratoga 10.00, returning 5.30 p.m. 'stopping at the lake', plus the annual Fitchburg excursion to Saratoga of 18 Aug 1894 from Greenfield and stations west (Bennington Semi-Weekly Banner 3 Aug 1894). Excursion specials are passenger service (Rule 1). Fitchburg passenger trains on this branch almost certainly ran wider, across 1887-1900, but no timetable was seen and 1894 is the only confirmed year; do not widen without a source. (The same advertisement's 'electric cars between Saratoga and Saratoga Lake' were a separate street railway.) headway_min is a placeholder for excursion-only evidence, not a measured frequency.

segments.note: Report block [11]. [ANCHOR] [OPEN] -- a single proven year, and the last confirmed one. The Boston and Maine ran an excursion from Worcester to Saratoga on Saturday 17 Aug 1901, leaving Worcester 7.10 a.m. and Saratoga 5.30 p.m. (Worcester Spy 14 Aug 1901). That it used this branch rather than the D&H is PRESUMED, not stated. Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed: B&M station lists of 1906-1941 are not passenger evidence, and the branch's 1955-57 abandonment (after the freight-only Saratoga & Schuylerville of 1946) gives track dates, not passenger dates.
